definitions.explanation: A person who hunts wild animals, either professionally or as a livelihood. Often appears in folk tales and stories about rural mountain life.

examples.japanese: {猟師|りょうし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{山|やま}→山：02168_yama⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|はい}った→入る：00494_hairu⟧。
examples.english: The hunter went into the mountains.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖父|そふ}→祖父：01452_sofu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{若|わか}い{頃|ころ}、{猟師|りょうし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦していた→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: My grandfather was a hunter when he was young.

examples.japanese: ⟦{昔話|むかしばなし}→昔話：12718_mukashibanashi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{熊|くま}→熊：04343_kuma⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{退治|たいじ}する→退治する：25396_taijisuru⟧{猟師|りょうし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{登場|とうじょう}→登場：13625_toujou⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Hunters who slay bears often appear in old folk tales.

notes:
Combines {猟|りょう} (hunting) and {師|し} (master/professional), indicating someone who hunts as a profession or calling. The word frequently appears in Japanese folk tales and stories about mountain village life.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {猟師|りょうし}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{小屋|こや}→小屋：02768_koya⟧: hunter's hut
- {猟師|りょうし}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: become a hunter
- {猟師|りょうし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: work as a hunter
- ⟦{山|やま}→山：02168_yama⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{猟師|りょうし}: mountain hunter

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japanese folk tales (⟦{昔話|むかしばなし}→昔話：12718_mukashibanashi⟧), the {猟師|りょうし} is a common character type, often depicted as brave and knowledgeable about the mountains. In modern Japan, the number of hunters has declined significantly, and {猟師|りょうし} now sometimes refers to people involved in ⟦{害獣|がいじゅう}{駆除|くじょ}→害獣駆除：29336_gaijuukujo⟧ (pest animal control) to manage wildlife like deer and boar that damage crops.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ハンター: hunter — the English loanword, used more casually and in modern/sport hunting contexts
- ⟦{漁師|りょうし}→漁師：21205_ryoushi⟧: fisherman — a homophone with the same reading but written with {漁|りょう} (fishing) instead of {猟|りょう} (hunting)
